newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BERLUSCONI CHIDES MILAN FANS, BACKS TABAREZ.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BERLUSCONI CHIDES MILAN FANS, BACKS TABAREZ.

text.p: Silvio Berlusconi, the billionaire owner of Italian champions AC Milan, has slammed his club's supporters for their lack of passion while ruling out any possibility of a change of coach this season.
Newspapers quoted the former Italian prime minister as saying the crowd of around 30,000 at San Siro for Wednesday's Champions' League clash with Sweden's IFK Gothenburg was a big disappointment.
The stadium seats 85,000 and Milan can, in a good season, regularly count on double Wednesday's turnout.
On Wednesday night there were boos and whistles for the home team, with bottles also reportedly thrown.

"I must make an appeal to Milan fans," said Berlusconi after the match, won 4-2 by Milan. "Those who really love the team should pull together around it, should come to matches and help us carry the financial sacrifices.
"Otherwise it will be illogical to continue making an effort to keep Milan on top of world soccer."
Milan, five times winners of the European Cup, have lost two of their four Champions' league matches this season and have been off the pace in serie A as well.
Berlusconi insisted that Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez, who took over from the highly successful Fabio Capello this season, had his full backing and would not be replaced.
"There is not the slightest chance that Milan will replace its coach this year," he said.
"I believe Tabarez is the right person to lead Milan to great achievements even during this season. He is not in doubt, he is not the one who goes out and plays.
"Milan have had some bad luck and some bad refereeing decisions this season."
